name: Fial
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fial was a goddess of Ireland. The River Feale, whose channel runs into the Shannon, took her name, and she watched over the water and the whole watershed. She therefore stood as a deity of fertility and plenty. The same name also went to one of Macha's daughters. That Macha died in labor soon after the twins came into the world, the girl Fial and the boy Fall.

attributes.attribute: empties into the Shannon and bears her name

okr.objective: Fial is an Irish river goddess of the River Feale and a daughter of Macha.
